Yes. The subtext enriches the story naturally rather than feeling forced. Jonas’s hesitation at the ramp, “als bräuchte er ein Ticket,” suggests estrangement from his mother and his childhood home. His assessing gaze and questions about ferry traffic hint at tension between his practical outlook and Ilse’s attachment to her work.

Most tellingly, Ilse notices his exhaustion and closes the ferry early without discussing his troubles. Her understated “Wasser aufsetzen” communicates care through action rather than an explicit declaration. The ferry’s routines and physical details make that gesture especially meaningful: she interrupts an established duty to make room for her son.
